# Appeal of Denial — Lower Back Disc Surgery / Decompression (CPT 63030)

**Member:** Morgan Foster
**Member ID:** W162894592
**Plan:** Ambetter (Commercial/ACA), Illinois
**Denial Date:** 2026-08-23
**Reference Number:** POC-F4C641ED8B-99591
**Governing Policy:** Clinical Policy: Disc Decompression Procedures (CP.MP.114) — https://www.ambetterhealth.com/content/dam/centene/ambetteril/clinical-policies/CP.MP.114.pdf

Dear Ambetter Appeals Department,

I am appealing the denial of coverage for lower back disc surgery/decompression (CPT 63030), which my surgeon, Dr. Reyes, has documented as medically necessary for my condition. I am requesting reconsideration of this decision.

## Why I believe this procedure meets the plan's own criteria

The denial states that my requested procedure does not meet the plan's medical necessity criteria. I have reviewed the plan's own policy, CP.MP.114, and I believe my medical records show that I meet the criteria the plan has published.

The policy states that "discectomy are medically necessary when meeting all of the following:"

**1. Nerve root compression confirmed by imaging**

The policy requires "Ne rve root compression confirmed by imaging and one of the following:"

My MRI of the lumbar spine, dated 2026-06-26, shows an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root. This is imaging-confirmed nerve root compression at a specific, named level.

**2. Radiculopathy with sensory deficit in a nerve root distribution**

My records document radicular pain extending into my right calf and positive provocative testing on the affected side, corresponding to the L5 nerve root level shown on imaging. This is consistent with pain in a nerve root distribution, which the policy addresses under "Radiculopathy with sensory deficit as evidenced by pain, parasthesias or numbness in a nerve root distribution."

**3. Failure of conservative therapy within the last year**

The policy states that the "Member/enrollee has failed to respond to conservative therapy, within the last year, including all of the following," and specifically requires "a) ≥ four wee ks physical therapy or prescribed home exercise program, or documentation of member/enrollee's inability to tolerate."

My records show:

- **Physical therapy:** I completed 18 supervised physical therapy visits over 12 weeks, from 2026-04-24 to 2026-07-17, including core stabilization and lumbar flexibility work, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note. This exceeds the four-week minimum.
- **Medication:** I took NSAIDs for 6 months with inadequate relief.
- **Injection:** I received a corticosteroid (epidural steroid) injection on 2026-06-17, which gave only 4 weeks of partial relief.
- **Activity modification:** My symptoms have persisted for 24 months of progressive pain despite these measures, and I currently cannot stand for more than 10 minutes.

I understand the policy also lists additional conservative-care elements, including a period of activity modification and use of NSAIDs or acetaminophen for a minimum duration unless contraindicated. I have not been given the plan's exact wording for those specific provisions, so I am not quoting them here, but I believe the record above — 12 weeks of supervised therapy, 6 months of NSAID use, and an epidural steroid injection — reflects a sustained and complete course of conservative treatment consistent with the policy's intent.

## Summary

Based on the plan's own published criteria in CP.MP.114, and the medical evidence in my file — imaging-confirmed L5 nerve root compression, radicular pain in a corresponding nerve root distribution, and a documented, extended course of conservative treatment that did not resolve my symptoms — I believe this request should meet the plan's medical necessity standard. My surgeon, Dr. Reyes, has determined that this procedure is medically necessary for my condition.

## What I am asking

I am asking Ambetter to reconsider this denial and approve coverage for CPT 63030 based on the records described above. If any additional documentation is needed from my surgeon's office to complete this review, please let me know specifically what is missing so it can be provided.

I understand my appeal must be received by 2027-02-19, though I understand the date printed on my denial letter is the authoritative deadline. I am submitting this appeal through the Illinois appeal process at ambetterhealth.com, and/or to the address listed on my denial notice.

Thank you for your time and reconsideration.

Sincerely,

Morgan Foster
Member ID: W162894592
[Signature]
[Date]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
